Frequently Asked Questions

Is it worth putting central heat and air in an older Liberty home for the first time?

Often yes, and ductless systems changed that math. Mini-splits deliver modern efficiency without the cost and disruption of retrofitting full ductwork into a house never built for it. A load calculation and a walkthrough determine whether ductless, ducted, or a mix fits the structure best.

How can I tell if my home’s wiring needs replacing rather than repairing?

The pattern tells more than any single symptom. One faulty outlet is a repair; recurring trips, warmth at multiple receptacles, and flickering across rooms point to the runs or the panel. An evaluation maps the system’s condition so the answer comes from evidence, and rewiring gets scoped only where it is actually needed.

What should I do the moment I suspect a frozen pipe?

Shut off water at the main and open the affected faucets to relieve pressure, then get a plumber moving. A frozen pipe that has not burst can often be thawed safely, while one that has will flood the moment it thaws. Speed decides which situation you are in when the water comes back on.

Why is my house so dry every winter?

Heating drops indoor relative humidity, and older construction compounds it by exchanging more air with the cold, dry outdoors. Every exchange trades away moisture. A whole-home humidifier meters it back at the equipment, which steadies the entire house instead of one room with a portable unit.

Do you serve the communities around Liberty?

Yes. Easley, Powdersville, and Piedmont sit on the same routes, and the website chat can confirm any Pickens County address quickly.
